title: Discrete Boltzmann Modeling of Sediment Transport in Dam‐Break Flows Over Erodible Beds
content:
Abstract

In this work, a discrete Boltzmann model (DBM) framework is developed for simulating sediment transport in dam-break flows considering both bedload and suspended sediment transport processes. To simulate the hydrodynamics where supercritical flows could be occurring, a DBM is used where its convective term is discretized using the second-order non-oscillatory and parameter-free dissipation scheme, and the temporal term is discretized by the first-order Euler method. For sediment transport, the standard lattice Boltzmann model is used to solve the governing equations for both suspended and bed loads, namely the advection-diffusion and Exner equations, respectively. The framework is validated against a series of one- and two-dimensional mobile-bed dam-break test cases. The numerical results show that the model effectively captures the complex water-sediment-bed interactions, even under strongly nonlinear conditions like supercritical flow.
